I found no real deviations on either floor, so the model passes. The numeric check passed with nothing flagged. It covered 743 nodes: 79 spaces, 85 openings, 2 connectors and 505 assets. The room proportions match, and so do the four exterior doors (top of H-B5, two on the left of H-C3 and H-C2, top of the corridor). The side doors from 0.33 to H-A4 and from 0.19 to H-A1 are also in place. My count of openings from the dataset plan, across both floors, comes to 85, which matches the numeric check. Floor 1 (level 1): corridor 1.01 with rooms 1.04-1.18 and 1.02, 1.03, 1.19-1.32 matches the dataset layout and room sizes, and every room has its corridor door. The dataset plans don't show equipment, so I relied on the numeric check for asset positions; it found no errors in position, rotation, scale or height. The B-column halls are almost empty in the generated plan, which looks plausible for halls that act as through-routes, and it is consistent with the matched asset count. A few assets sit right against walls, for example one in room 1.10 that reaches slightly into the corridor. Their positions are exactly the dataset's, so I didn't count them as deviations. Fill colours and label positions differ between the two plans, but that is styling only.
